descriptionChirho: A portable sleeping mat or simple bed, the kind used by the poor or sick, prominently featured in healing narratives where Jesus commands the healed to 'take up your mat' (Mark 2:4-12, John 5:8-11, Acts 5:15, 9:33). All three clusters are inflectional variants of the same noun krabbatos in singular and plural, various cases (accusative singular, genitive singular, genitive plural, dative plural). Eng 'mat / mats,' spa 'catre / camilla / lechos / camillas,' hin khaat / khatiya, arb sariir / furush / as-surur, kor chimsang / chimsangdeul, swa kitanda / mikeka / vitanda. The Swahili shift from kitanda (bed) to mikeka (mats) reflects register, not meaning.
